evidence: Plan item 2.5 (docs/AGENT_PLAN.md): the Displacement Directions page opened at nu = 10 with 2 smoothing passes, while analyze_displacement_directions lets the engine choose the tiling (recommendedFrequency: the finest nu whose cells still average at least 12 displacements) and never smooths, so a user, arm A and the Copilot read one site on two tilings: on dev-thermal-null's three flattened O sites (512 copies) the map test read 2.32, 2.16 and 2.23 sigma on the page against 7.17, 6.30 and 7.13 sigma on the tool (nu = 2). Every number the page shows or arm A reads, checked against the smoothing: the map test, the +u/-u asymmetry and its null, the Bingham anisotropy, and the hover's counts and local z come from the raw counts or the vectors and do not move with it; but both engines pick the peak cell on the smoothed enhancement, so the peak's cell, direction, enhancement, tie count and sigma did (the test applies the picked cell's raw count, conservative whichever cell is picked, but not the tool's cell). At the old default (nu = 10, 2 passes against 0) dev-zone-boundary's O site 5 read -10.4 against -0.28 sigma (the smoothed peak cell held 2 raw atoms, the fullest 4) and dev-offcentre's K site 1 -5.63 against -3.06 sigma in another direction; on the engine's own tiling with 2 passes dev-thermal-null's Ti read -2.06 against -0.69 sigma at a direction 90 deg away, dev-offcentre's K -2.88 against -1.33 sigma with x and y reversed, and a judgment case's split site put its peak in the antipodal cell. The colorbar's maximum and the hover's enhancement and mean |dr| describe the drawn map and stay smoothed with it. The change: the page opens at Auto, the engine's resolution, with the nu it chose in the Auto choice's label; every readout is the raw histogram's at the page's analysis settings (smoothing 0, the tool's request); the map is the same request smoothed; arm A reads the page's own defaults (src/directionSettings.js). Known answer (validation/__tests__/directionsDefault.test.js): on every site of dev-thermal-null the page's default readout equals the tool's result field for field and arm A's reading equals the tool's numbers; the O sites clear 3 sigma on the map test and were below it on the old default; with 2 passes the counts, map, asymmetry and Bingham tests are unchanged and the peak cell moves on at least one site. Arms A and A+ on the dev set before and after: every D record identical, and every score of the ten paired cases; nine records move, each through a split site's Displacement Directions reading, which now records the nu it read. dev-offcentre A and A+: Nb 4.33 -> 17.2 sigma at nu = 2, the claim's direction [0.1 0.06 -1] -> [0 0 -1] (within tolerance before and after). dev-zone-boundary A: the Ti peak's significance rises from 2.3 to 5.4 sigma, now significant, so the spurious off_centre Ti names the peak [0 0 1] instead of PC1's [-0.03 0.1 1]; the same score. dev-jahn-teller A and A+: F 2.71 -> 6.58 sigma at nu = 1, the tolerated off_centre F names the coarse peak [-1 0 -0.62] instead of PC1's [1 0 -0.01]; the same scores. Two judgment cases move (their values in validation/baseline/arm-a-dev.json and the arms.test.js pins): on dev-jt-off-centre a split site small enough for Auto's nu = 1 (twelve cells whose centres lie 31.7 deg from every cube axis, so an axial lobe falls on a cell boundary) now reads a significant peak 31.7 deg off its planted axis, beyond the 15 deg tolerance, and arm A, which takes that peak, scores its off-centre direction off, a side miss beside the case's situation (A+ takes PC1 there since part 2); on dev-octahedral-clusters the tolerated claim names the other end of the same axis. The dev thermal case's own records do not move: the arms read the direction map of split sites only, and it has none. Part 2, #110's two questions, decided by the manager on the user's delegation, 2026-10-19. (1) The direction resolution is a measurement limit, so it is reported: peakDirection is the peak cell's centre, and both engines now return the peak cell's circumscribed radius, peakCellRadiusDeg, the largest angle from the cell's centre to its own vertices (atan2(|c x v|, c . v)), so every direction assigned to the cell lies within it (the equal-area cap, 33.6 deg at nu = 1, would leave the cell's corners outside and understate the bound). It is 37.4 deg for every cell at nu = 1 (the dodecahedron's closed form, arccos sqrt((5 + 2 sqrt 5) / 15)), 19.3-20.9 deg at nu = 2 and 12.3-13.7 deg at nu = 3, so the 15 deg line (LOW_INDEX_CONE_DEG) falls between nu = 2 and 3; on Auto every site under 1104 copies gets nu <= 2, and the Demo's 52 sites (1000 copies, nu = 2) read 19.3 or 20.9 deg. The golden pins the field in both runtimes, with rule tests in both suites (the closed form, every assigned direction within its cell's radius, the 15 deg line). The tool gives peak.radius_deg and a significant peak as '[u v w] +- R deg, the cell radius at nu = n'; above 15 deg (directionResolved) it says 'The direction is not resolved finer than R deg (over 15 deg), so it names no <100>, <110> or <111> family.' and the map check says the peak places the direction only to within its cell; the page prints the same '+- R deg, the cell radius at nu = n' beside the peak. Known answer (src/__tests__/directionResolution.test.js): 216 copies of a planted [0 0 1] split site read nu = 1, a 37.4 deg radius, a significant peak whose cell centre sits 31.7 deg off the axis (within its radius), the unresolved wording and no family named; 4000 copies of the same site read nu = 5, a radius under 15 deg and the resolved wording, the centre within its radius of the axis. (2) Arm A+ applies the stated bound: a significant peak in a cell wider than 15 deg gives way to PC1 (SWEEP_RULES.directionResolved, the tool's rule), since a cell cannot localise a direction more finely than its own size; arm A keeps reading the default page as a user would and takes the peak. The page's new text changes what arm A records, not what it claims: its reading now carries the radius it shows. (3) The map opens unsmoothed (smoothing 0, was 2), UI only: no readout or score depends on it. Arms A and A+ on the dev set before and after part 2: the same nine records move. Arm A's five gain the radius in their readings and keep every claim and score, dev-jt-off-centre's lowered one included. A+'s four take PC1, every dev split site's peak cell being nu <= 2: dev-offcentre's Nb [0 0 -1] -> [0 -0.01 1] (the same axis, accurate both ways), dev-jahn-teller's F [-1 0 -0.62] -> [1 0 -0.01] and dev-octahedral-clusters' W [-1 0 0] -> [1 0 0] (tolerated claims), and the judgment case's Ag back to PC1, within 2 deg of its axis, so A+'s score there is again its pre-2.5 one; every A+ score now equals its pre-2.5 value. What the model sees changes in analyze_displacement_directions only: its description names the radius (+21 characters a request; the context budget's worst turns +8 to +9 tokens) and its result gives peak.radius_deg and a longer note (the Demo's site 1 result +109 characters); the model-visible snapshots, the validation record snapshots and the budget pins are updated for it, and facts are unchanged. The test set was not run. Approved by the manager on the user's delegation, 2026-10-19.
proposed_fix: The page and the tool at the same settings: the Displacement Directions page opens at Auto, the engine's recommended frequency (the tiling analyze_displacement_directions reads), and labels the Auto choice with the nu it chose for the site on screen; a picked resolution overrides it and stays as every option on the page does (page state: kept across a site change, a tab switch and another run; a Copilot step's Show in still sets it). Every readout under the sphere comes from the raw histogram at the page's analysis settings (smoothing 0); the sphere, its colorbar and the hover draw the same request at the page's smoothing, which opens at 0, so smoothing stays a display setting. One module holds the defaults and both requests (src/directionSettings.js; src/useDirectionHistogram.js asks for both, and only for the map on a smoothing change); arm A, and A+ through the same reading, reads the page's defaults from it (ARM_A_RULES.DIRECTION_SETTINGS is DIRECTION_DEFAULTS). The direction resolution: both engines return peakCellRadiusDeg, the peak cell's circumscribed radius; the tool (peak.radius_deg) and the page give the peak direction '+- R deg, the cell radius at nu = n', and above LOW_INDEX_CONE_DEG the tool calls it not resolved finer than R and names no low-index family; arm A+ takes PC1 over a peak whose cell is wider than 15 deg (directionResolved), arm A reads the page as a user would, and both record the radius. PROTOCOL_VERSION 2026-10-19.17; the moved dev records re-recorded in validation/baseline/arm-a-dev.json, the others as recorded. Left open for the user: the displacement-anisotropy skill still says the page defaults to nu = 10, smoothed (SKILL.md lines 49 and 74-75), for the skill fact-sync PR (the skills are what the model reads, so not edited here). Commits bc30982 (the default), 9c9cc7a (the engines' radius), 4370616 (the tool, the page, A+ and the smoothing), 385aad8 (the protocol renumbered). Approved by the manager on the user's delegation, 2026-10-19.
